summary: The design is a sound rewrite: one cluster launch replaces 5 launches on batched shapes and the 10.3 us Triton kernel at decode_1, with no rules problems, and its 6-12 us targets look reachable against 0.1-3.7 us floors. Two spec defects need fixing before building. The softmax scale applies qk_scale_factor twice, which the self-check would catch, silently disabling the path and wasting the stage. The smem/occupancy budget is understated: the 'one wave at B=32' claim does not hold if the f16 V copy and the fp32 partials take their own smem.
justification: Mechanism: FINDINGS backs it. Every sliding shape is dominated by fixed-cost chains, not bytes. decode_16: FA3 main 9.9 + combine 3.3 + prepare 1.8 + pre-attn + norm-gate = 20.8 us against a 1.6 us floor. verify_1: 7.4 + 3.8 + 1.8 = 17.6 us against 0.1 us. decode_1: a single 10.3 us Triton kernel against 0.1 us, using a ticket/fence global merge and half-row (64 B) gathers. Collapsing to one kernel with the merge in DSMEM removes the combine, prepare and norm-gate launches plus the global round trip, so the 'expected faster' directions on all six sliding shapes agree with the weights (46 each) and floors in TASK.md. Full shapes flat is right, since the gate is config-only and the module is separate. Data volume is small: 2047 x 256 B = 524 KB per request, 16.8 MB at B=32, about 3.5 us at 4.8 TB/s. The decode_32/verify_32 targets of ~9.5-12 us are therefore plausible, decode_1 <= 4.5 us is plausible (16 CTAs x ~33 KB each, ~1-1.5 us cold gather), and the speedup arithmetic (sliding share 59-63% of the B=1 loads) holds. WEAKEST LINKS: (1) A correctness defect in the spec. q is multiplied by qk_scale_factor before E4M3 rounding, and then the score scale is again sm_scale * qk_scale_factor * log2e * k_scale. That is 5.473 applied twice. Master's Triton kernel uses q*q_scale with score_scale = sm_scale*LOG2E. The splitkv path folds 5.473 into the scale and does not scale q. Pick one convention. As written, the self-check fails, _SLIDE_OK clears, every sliding shape runs master, and stage 1 reads as flat with no information. (2) Smem and occupancy. The 66 KB figure counts only the fp8 K+V gather (256 B/token x ~256-264 tokens, plus 16 B pads, ~74 KB at L=8 with the last rank's extra rows). It leaves out three things: the f16 V copy (+~67 KB), the fp32 (m, l, acc) partials for R=16L rows (L=8: 128 x 64 x 4 = 32 KB) and the q operand. That is ~175-180 KB per CTA, so 1 CTA/SM. Clusters of 8 must also co-reside in one GPC (H200 GPCs hold ~16-18 SMs), so the B=32 grid of 32 clusters x 8 CTAs likely cannot be resident at once (roughly 14-16 clusters active). It would run 2+ waves and miss the ~9.5/12 us targets. Fix: alias the partials over the consumed K region, and convert V fp8->f16 into registers per fragment instead of a full f16 smem copy. That gets under ~113 KB for 2 CTAs/SM. Also log cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters for C=8 at the actual smem size. (3) Minor wording: page-table cp.async loads must complete (wait_group) before the dependent KV gather is issued. 'All issued before any wait' cannot literally hold, but the intended one-index-round-trip chain is right. (4) The m16n8k32 e4m3 mma.sync needs PTX ISA 8.4 / CUDA >= 12.4 for sm_90a. The separate module plus per-L fallback covers a build failure, but a fallback again reads as flat. The log must show the build result so a flat headline is not misread as 'design does not help'.
confounders: None from the landed list (empty). Master's own sliding path is the incumbent: the Triton _sliding_fused_kernel at decode_1, FA3 elsewhere. The stage is judged per shape on kernel time against it, so no landed-change interaction applies.

Not landed but relevant to judging: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv (running) and sliding-verify-cuda-streamk-window (queued) may move the incumbent on batched decode/verify sliding shapes before dispatch. Compare against the master profile at dispatch time, as the risk section says, not against the FINDINGS numbers quoted in the milestones.
interference: No companions. It is a kind: rewrite judged on its own kernel time per shape (profile top_kernels shows sliding_cluster_kernel as the only kernel against the incumbent sum), so attribution is direct and needs no A/B. Nothing has landed that could confound it. The one ambiguity a single run can produce is 'flat everywhere'. That would mean the self-check fell back (likely given the double-scale defect) or the module failed to build, not that the design lost. The required log lines (build seconds, chosen C, self-check rel L2 per L, and which path each sliding shape took) settle that without an extra run. Stage 2 is the follow-up for tuning C and smem.
rules_flags: No rule violations found in the design. The gate and C are config-only. cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters runs at import, not in the timed call. There is no workspace and no host sync. The self-check uses synthetic data at import. E4M3 query rounding is allowed (as FA3), and V widened to f16 is finer than FP8. Every window key is scored with per-row masking, and the new keys are attended from smem, not skipped.

Precision note, not a violation: the q E4M3 rounding happens after the 5.473 multiply. That has the same relative precision as FA3's rounding of the unscaled q, and master's Triton path also rounds after the factor (to bf16). Make sure the score scale then omits qk_scale_factor (see justification).

Budget risk: a second load_inline module (splitkv already takes ~41.5 s per the profile logs) plus two import-time self-checks run inside the 15-minute run limit. Keep the template instantiations to L in {1,8} and log the build time, so a timeout is not charged as a failure.
open_questions: Which scale convention will be built: q*5.473 then E4M3 with scale = sm_scale*log2e*k_scale, or unscaled E4M3 q with scale = sm_scale*qk_scale_factor*log2e*k_scale? The spec currently does both.

What is the real per-CTA smem at L=8 for the last rank (256 old + 8 new rows, f16 V copy, partials, q operand)? What does cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters return for C=8 at that size? Does B=32 fit in one wave?
Is the toolkit on the judge >= CUDA 12.4 (PTX 8.4) so m16n8k32 e4m3 mma.sync compiles for sm_90a? If not, is there an f16/bf16 QK fallback in the same module, rather than falling back to master?

At B=1, C=16 uses only 16 SMs, against the incumbent's 32 CTAs. Is the cold gather of ~33 KB per CTA latency-bound enough that C=16 with 2 CTAs/SM, or multi-stage cp.async, matters for the <= 4.5 us target?

For the test cases with ctx < window (batch 1 ctx 10 is page 64 and stays on master, but the self-check's seq_len 10 hits the new kernel), most ranks have empty chunks. Confirm that the m = -inf partials get weight 0 in the DSMEM merge, as master's combine does.
